extra_quotes: The electronic structures of bulk zinc-blende GaAs and diamond Si were calculated within density-functional theory(DFT)[33,34], usingtheall-electronfull-potential linearized augmented-plane-wave method implemented in WIEN2k [35].
Using the calculated DFT electronic structures, we evaluated the Hall and magneto-optical responses within the linear-response formalism [40–43].
We calculate the inverse Faraday effect using the second-order density-matrix formalism employed in Ref. [29].
Since phonon-assisted transitions, which govern the indirect absorption onset of Si, are not included [50, 51], the indirect gap does not produce a distinct feature in the calculated response.

The calculated spectral features are shifted toward lower photon energies relative to experiment, because the PBE exchange-correlation functional underestimates the relevant interband energy separations [53].
